title: Local rigidity of morphisms to a fine affine fan from section germs
statement:
Let $(T,\mathcal A)$ be a topological space with a sheaf of commutative monoids whose stalks are sharp, let $P$ be a fine sharp monoid, and put $S(P)=(\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}P,\overline{\widetilde P})$, with these notions and local monoidal-space morphisms as in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Let $V\subseteq T$ be open, let $t\in V$, and let $h,k:(V,\mathcal A|_V)\to S(P)$ be local morphisms of monoidal spaces, i.e. their stalk homomorphisms are local. Denote their pullbacks of canonical monoid sections by $\rho_h,\rho_k:P\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal A)$. If
$$\operatorname{germ}_t(\rho_h(p))=\operatorname{germ}_t(\rho_k(p))\quad\text{for every }p\in P,$$
then there is an open neighborhood $U$ of $t$ with $U\subseteq V$ such that $\rho_h|_U=\rho_k|_U$ and $h|_U=k|_U$ as morphisms of monoidal spaces, including both their continuous maps and their sheaf homomorphisms. The assertion also holds for the trivial monoid $P=\{0\}$, without choosing any generators.

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of Theorem 3.3.15, printed p.109, sentence shrinking U because the monoids are fine and subsequent invocation of Lemma 3.1.8(ii), printed p.99; formulated for arbitrary sharp monoidal spaces.

proof.text: If $P=\{0\}$, set $U=V$; both homomorphisms take $0$ to the zero section, so $\rho_h|_U=\rho_k|_U$, without choosing generators. Otherwise, fineness in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] supplies a finite generating set $E\subset P$. For each $e\in E$, equality of the two germs at $t$ means, by the explicit equivalence relation defining stalks in that definition, that there is an open $U_e$ with $t\in U_e\subseteq V$ on which $\rho_h(e)$ and $\rho_k(e)$ restrict equally. Put $U=\bigcap_{e\in E}U_e$. This finite intersection is open, contains $t$, and lies in $V$. Restricting each equality further gives equality on every generator over $U$.

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of Theorem 3.3.15, printed p.109, sentence “Since the monoids are fine, we can shrink U”; finite-generator and germ argument made explicit.

proof.text: In the nontrivial case, every $p\in P$ is a finite sum $e_1+\cdots+e_r$ of elements of $E$, allowing repetitions and the empty sum. Since restriction maps and $\rho_h,\rho_k$ are monoid homomorphisms, the two images of this sum over $U$ are the sums of the images of the $e_i$. Induction on $r$ gives equality: for $r=0$ both images are zero, and adjoining $e_{r+1}$ preserves equality by Step 1 and additivity. Hence $\rho_h|_U=\rho_k|_U$ as homomorphisms on all of $P$. Together with the trivial case of Step 1, this proves the section assertion in every case.

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of Theorem 3.3.15, printed p.109, same shrinking sentence; extension from generators by additivity.

proof.text: The restrictions $h|_U,k|_U$ are local morphisms: their stalk maps at $x\in U$ are the original ones. Indeed, intersecting representative neighborhoods with the open set $U$ identifies the stalk of $\mathcal A|_U$ at $x$ with $\mathcal A_x$ under the germ definition of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Thus these stalks remain sharp. Pullback of each canonical section along $h|_U$ is $\rho_h(p)|_U$, and along $k|_U$ is $\rho_k(p)|_U$, by compatibility of sheaf maps with restriction. Apply the last assertion of [lem-trf-affine-fan-canonical-section-rigidity] to the source $(U,\mathcal A|_U)$ and the fine sharp monoid $P$. Step 2 (or the trivial case of Step 1) supplies its equality of canonical-section homomorphisms. It yields $h|_U=k|_U$ as morphisms, including both the continuous maps and the sheaf homomorphisms.
